## Mathematical Review

# Critic Analysis — prob-01

**Problem:** *Descriptive Aspects of Structures with Countable Automorphism Groups*
(Kalociński & Slaman). Question 1.2.

**Status of attempt:** No `solution.tex` exists. No prior `docs_*.md` files are present in
the workspace (the referenced `docs_index.txt` is absent). This analysis is therefore built
from the problem statement alone.

---

## Background

We work with countably infinite first-order structures whose universe is $\N$ and whose
symbols are interpreted by elements / total functions / relations on $\N$ (a *representation*).
$\AUT(\A)$ is the automorphism group. The key definitions:

- **Computably $\AUT$-countable on a cone.** There is an oracle $C$ such that for *every*
  copy $\B \cong \A$, every $\sigma\in\AUT(\B)$ is computable from $\B\oplus C$.
- **$\Sigma^{in}_1$-definability.** $f:\A\to\A$ is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from parameters
  $\bar a$ if there is a *family* of existential (computable infinitary $\Sigma_1$) formulas
  $(\phi_i)_{i\in\N}$ with $f(x)=y \iff \exists i\,\A\models\phi_i(\bar a,x,y)$. Equivalently the
  graph of $f$ is a c.e. (over a cone) union of existentially-definable sets with parameters
  $\bar a$.

Relevant cited results:

- **Theorem 2.2 (Hodges, *Model Theory* Cor. 4.2.5).** If $\A$ is countable and $\AUT(\A)$ is
  countable, then there is a *single* finite tuple $\bar a$ such that every automorphism is
  determined by its action on $\bar a$ (i.e. the pointwise stabilizer of $\bar a$ is trivial).
  This is a consequence of the topological fact that a countable closed subgroup of $S_\infty$
  has an open point-stabilizer that is trivial along some finite tuple; more precisely a
  countable Polish group with a comeager orbit / Baire-category argument forces some basic open
  set (a stabilizer of a finite tuple) to be a singleton in the group.

- **Theorem 2.3 (after Ash–Knight–Manasse–Slaman 1989).** $\A$ is computably $\AUT$-countable on
  a cone **iff** for each $\pi\in\AUT(\A)$ there is *some* finite $\bar a$ (depending on $\pi$)
  such that $\pi$ is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar a$. The engine is the AKMS theorem:
  a relation $R$ is *c.e. on a cone* iff it is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable with finitely many
  parameters. Applying this to the graph of an automorphism converts the relativized-computation
  statement into a definability statement.

The **gap between 2.2 and 2.3** is the crux. Theorem 2.2 gives *uniform* parameters (one tuple
works for all $\pi$, and only "determines" $\pi$, not "defines" it effectively). Theorem 2.3
gives *effective* (definability) parameters but they depend on $\pi$. The Question asks whether
effectivity + uniformity can fail simultaneously, in the strong sense that **no** finite tuple
$\bar a$ can effectively define all automorphisms — and indeed for each $\bar a$ there is a
$\pi$ defeating it even when one is *allowed to add the images* $\pi(\bar a)$ to the parameters.

---

## Proof Structure

A complete solution must **construct** an explicit computably-represented structure $\A$ and
prove two clauses.

**(P1) Positive clause:** $\A$ is computably $\AUT$-countable on a cone. By Theorem 2.3 it
suffices to show: for each $\pi\in\AUT(\A)$ there is a finite tuple $\bar a$ with $\pi$
$\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar a$. (Equivalently, build $\A$ so that any copy can compute
its automorphisms from a fixed oracle.) One must also confirm $\AUT(\A)$ is countable
(otherwise the framing collapses) — typically by exhibiting $\AUT(\A)$ concretely.

**(P2) Negative / diagonal clause:** For every finite $\bar a\subseteq\A$ there exists
$\pi\in\AUT(\A)$ such that $\pi$ is **not** $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from
$\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$. This is the hard, anti-uniformity part. It must hold for *all* finite
tuples simultaneously, so the construction must contain "enough room" / arbitrarily complex
automorphisms beyond any finite parameter horizon.

**(P3) Computable representation:** the chosen $\A$ must actually admit a computable copy
(domain $\N$, all functions/relations computable), since "computably-represented" is required.

Glue: (P1)+(P2)+(P3) together answer the Question affirmatively (such $\A$ exists).

---

## Gap Analysis

Since there is no `solution.tex`, every component below is currently an **open sub-lemma**.
These are the genuine mathematical gaps a solver must close.

**G1 — Construct the witnessing structure $\A$ (with a computable copy).**
Need an explicit $\A$ whose automorphism group is countable yet "rich enough" along an infinite
sequence of independent coordinates. A natural candidate template: a disjoint union / tree of
infinitely many finite or finitely-generated rigidifiable "gadgets" $G_0,G_1,\dots$, where each
$G_n$ contributes one independent binary (or finite) automorphism degree of freedom, but the
gadgets are *individually rigid up to a single swap* and *globally only move finitely many at a
time* in a way that keeps $\AUT(\A)$ countable. The construction must be pinned down precisely.

**G2 — Prove $\AUT(\A)$ is countable.** The framing (Theorems 2.2, 2.3) requires countable
$\AUT(\A)$. With infinitely many independent binary choices one risks $\AUT(\A)\cong
(\Z/2)^\N$, which is *uncountable*. So the construction must force automorphisms to act
nontrivially on only finitely many coordinates (e.g. $\AUT(\A)\cong\bigoplus_n \Z/2 =$ the
*direct sum*, which is countable), or otherwise restrict to a countable group. Proving exactly
which permutations preserve all relations is a real lemma.

**G3 — Prove the positive clause (P1): every $\pi$ is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from finitely
many parameters.** Given G2 (each $\pi$ moves only finitely many gadgets), one needs to show that
fixing parameters witnessing the finite support of $\pi$ makes the graph of $\pi$
existentially definable (over a cone). This requires that within each gadget the swap is
existentially/computably describable once a base point is named.

**G4 — Prove the negative clause (P2): the anti-uniform diagonalization.** For an arbitrary
finite $\bar a$, exhibit $\pi$ with $\pi$ not $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from
$\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$. The subtlety: adding $\pi(\bar a)$ to the parameter set is a *gift to
the adversary*, so the gadgets must be designed so that naming $\bar a$ and $\pi(\bar a)$ still
leaves infinitely many gadgets "unaddressed", and on those unaddressed gadgets $\pi$ can encode
a non-$\Sigma^{in}_1$ (e.g. non-c.e.) amount of information. This needs (a) a coding of a
non-c.e. set into the action of $\pi$ on the gadgets outside the span of $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$,
and (b) an argument that $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definability of $\pi$ from those parameters would make
that set c.e.-on-a-cone, contradicting its choice.

**G5 — Reconcile G3 and G4 (consistency of P1 with P2).** This is the conceptual heart: each
individual $\pi$ has *some* finite defining tuple (P1), yet *no* fixed tuple defines all $\pi$,
and moreover for each tuple a defeating $\pi$ exists *even after augmenting with $\pi(\bar a)$*.
The construction must make the defining tuple of $\pi$ genuinely depend on data not recoverable
from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$. One must verify there is no hidden contradiction: e.g. show that
the tuple that defines a given $\pi$ in P1 is exactly "a base point inside each moved gadget",
information *not* supplied by an arbitrary externally-chosen $\bar a$.

---

## Difficulty Assessment

- **G1/G2 (moderate–hard):** Designing relations so that $\AUT(\A)$ is the *direct sum* of the
  per-gadget groups (finite support), not the *direct product*, is delicate. A connectedness /
  "linking" relation is usually needed to force finite support, but linking can accidentally
  rigidify the whole structure (killing G4) or create unexpected automorphisms (killing G2).
  Getting countability and richness simultaneously is the standard tension in such constructions.

- **G3 (moderate):** Standard once supports are finite, but "over a cone" subtleties and the
  *family* of formulas $(\phi_i)$ must be handled carefully; one must not assume a single
  existential formula suffices.

- **G4 (hard):** This is the diagonalization against *all* finite parameter tuples with the
  $\pi(\bar a)$ handicap. The key difficulty is that the parameters $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ are
  $2|\bar a|$ points that may "spend" gadget addresses; the coding must survive this. Producing a
  non-c.e./non-$\Sigma^{in}_1$ obstruction that is robust to adding $\pi(\bar a)$ requires a
  careful priority or coding argument and is the principal research content.

- **G5 (conceptual):** Must be argued explicitly to avoid the (very plausible-looking)
  impression that P1 and P2 are contradictory. This is exactly the "gap between Thm 2.2 and
  Thm 2.3" the authors highlight; the proof must show the construction lives precisely in that
  gap.

---

## Suggested Approaches

1. **Independent-gadget direct-sum construction.** Let $\A=\bigsqcup_n G_n$ with a coordinating
   relation that forces finite support. Each $G_n$ is a small structure with $\AUT(G_n)\cong
   \Z/2$ generated by an involution $\tau_n$ whose two swapped points are *not* existentially
   distinguishable without naming an external base point. Take $\AUT(\A)=\bigoplus_n\langle
   \tau_n\rangle$. Code a target set $X\subseteq\N$ into a candidate $\pi=\prod_{n\in X}\tau_n$
   restricted to finite support along subsequences; choose $X$ (relative to the cone) to be
   non-c.e. so that $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definability fails. To beat a given $\bar a$, work on gadgets
   with index above $\max$ of all gadget-indices touched by $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$.

2. **Coding via "twins" the parameters cannot resolve.** Engineer each gadget to contain a pair
   of automorphic points $\{p_n,q_n\}$ such that distinguishing them is exactly as hard as
   deciding $n\in X$; then $\pi$'s action (swap vs. fix) on the unaddressed gadgets encodes $X$,
   and $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definability of $\pi$ from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ would give a
   c.e.-on-a-cone description of $X$, contradicting non-c.e.-ness via the AKMS direction of
   Theorem 2.3.

3. **Priority / forcing for the negative clause.** If a direct coding is fragile under the
   $\pi(\bar a)$ handicap, run a finite-injury or forcing construction building $\A$ (or building
   the bad $X$ relative to a cone) to diagonalize against the $e$-th potential family of
   existential formulas, for each finite parameter tuple enumerated.

4. **Verify the positive clause via finite support directly:** prove each $\pi$ has finite
   support, name one base point per moved gadget, and write the explicit family $(\phi_i)$ that
   defines the within-gadget swap; conclude P1 from Theorem 2.3.

---

## References

- Prior docs: **none found** (`docs_index.txt` and `docs_*.md` absent from the workspace; this
  review is from `problem.tex` only).
- W. Hodges, *Model Theory*, Cambridge, 1993 — Cor. 4.2.5 (Theorem 2.2 here).
- Ash, Knight, Manasse, Slaman, "Generic copies of countable structures", APAL 1989 — the
  c.e.-on-a-cone $\Leftrightarrow$ $\Sigma^{in}_1$-with-parameters characterization (Theorem 2.3
  here).
- Background: $S_\infty$ as a Polish group; Baire-category / topological characterization of
  countable closed subgroups; computable infinitary $\Sigma_1$ formulas; Turing cones and
  cone-uniform (Martin-style) statements.

## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

**Verdict: the current attempt does NOT solve Question 1.2.** Sub-lemma G2 ($\AUT(\A)\cong\Z$) is correct, but the two halves of Sub-lemma G5 are mutually contradictory and the proof of the negative clause contains a concrete, fatal error. Two new gap issues filed: **prob-01-7** (fatal P1/P2 contradiction) and **prob-01-8** (the witness-confinement error in P2). These refine the open issues prob-01-5 and prob-01-6.

### Summary of the conflict
- **P1 (Lemma `lem:P1`) is correct:** the *oriented spine* $R$ lets a single anchor $(0,0)$ recover a base point $(n,0)$ in **every** gadget via $\mathrm{Base}_n$, so $\sigma^k$ is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from the single point $(0,0)$.
- **P2 (Lemma `lem:P2`) is therefore false:** take $\bar a=((0,0))$. As $\sigma$ fixes gadgets setwise, $\bar a\cup\sigma(\bar a)=\{(0,0),(0,1)\}\supseteq\{(0,0)\}$, so by P1 $\sigma$ IS definable from $\bar a\cup\sigma(\bar a)$, contradicting P2.

### The concrete error inside P2
The step $\A\models\phi_i(\bar c,x_0,y_0)\Rightarrow \A\models\phi_i(\bar c,\rho x_0,\rho y_0)$ relies on the false claim that existential witnesses stay in the $P$-component $G_{n_0}$. The spine $R$ connects $G_{n_0}$ to the directed anchor $D$ on $G_0$, so witnesses can read the global orientation. Moreover $\rho$ is an automorphism only of the *truncated* substructure $\bar c\cup G_{n_0}$ (R-edges deleted), **not** of $\A$ — numerically, $\rho$ breaks 48 R-edges on a finite model. So $\rho$ does not preserve $\phi_i$ in $\A$.

### Why this is a design-level failure (not a wording fix)
Any oriented coupling that (i) makes $\AUT$ countable by tying all gadgets to a fixed anchor *automatically* (ii) lets one parameter orient all gadgets, refuting P2. The genuine difficulty of Question 1.2 is to make the "which automorphism" datum **semantically present** (Theorem 2.2: one point determines $\pi$) yet **$\Sigma_1$-inaccessible** from externally chosen finite parameters (so P2 holds). The present spine design fails this.

### Suggested redesign directions
1. Abandon the oriented-spine-to-anchor coupling.
2. Encode the action so that orientation/direction is a $\Pi_1$/limit (non-existential) invariant, not certifiable by finitely many existential witnesses with parameters off a cofinal set of gadgets.
3. Any P2 proof must produce a genuine $\bar c$-fixing automorphism (or self-embedding) of the *full* $\A$ reversing the relevant action — forcing the construction to actually admit such maps.

Full details, background, and references in the attached **Critic Analysis** document. No prior `docs_*.md` files were present in the workspace.

## Mathematical Review (critic-agent) — current solution.tex

**Verdict: the current `solution.tex` does NOT answer Question 1.2.** It is a careful *negative* analysis: it correctly computes $\AUT(\A)\cong\Z$ (G2), correctly proves (P1) for its candidate $\A$, and then correctly proves that $\A$ **fails** (P2) (Lemma `lem:leak`, Cor. `cor:P2-fails`). The draft explicitly leaves the actual witnessing construction "as the outstanding task." So the central existence claim of Q1.2 is unproved.

What is sound and valuable in the draft:
- $\AUT(\A)\cong\Z$ via in/out-degree index recovery + path rigidity (I re-checked the argument; correct).
- The **embedding criterion** (Lemma `lem:embcrit`): if a global self-embedding $h$ fixes $\bar c$ pointwise and $h\pi\neq\pi h$, then $\pi$ is not $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar c$ (standard $\exists$-preservation; sound).
- The honest retraction of the earlier draft's two fatal errors (P1/P2 contradiction for the spine; the witness-confinement / non-global-$\rho$ error) — these match open issues prob-01-7, prob-01-8.

I numerically confirmed (truncation $0\le n\le4$, $|i|\le6$): $\sigma_k\in\AUT(\A)$ on the interior, and the leak family $\phi_n$ defines $\sigma$ parameter-free on the interior (0 mismatches). So the draft's negative conclusion about $\A$ is correct: $\A$ genuinely fails (P2).

**New gaps filed:** prob-01-9 (the unresolved YES/NO dichotomy — no witness exists, and the 'tension' in `rem:spec` is heuristic, not a no-go theorem) and prob-01-10 (any future P2 witness $h$ must be a GLOBAL self-embedding preserving+reflecting ALL relations incl. cross-gadget coupling edges — the precise obstruction that killed `def:A`). These refine the still-open sub-lemma issues prob-01-2/-4/-5/-6.

Full analysis (also attached as a linked doc):

# Critic Analysis — prob-01

**Problem:** *Descriptive Aspects of Structures with Countable Automorphism Groups*
(Kalociński & Slaman), Question 1.2.

**Status of attempt (solution.tex):** The file is **not a solution to Question 1.2**.
It is an extended *negative* analysis of a single candidate structure $\A$. It (correctly)
computes $\AUT(\A)\cong\Z$, (correctly) proves the positive clause (P1) for $\A$, and then
(correctly, with retractions of an earlier erroneous draft) proves that the candidate $\A$
**fails** the negative clause (P2). The document closes by reducing the problem to a
specification (Remark `rem:spec`) and explicitly leaving the actual construction "as the
outstanding task." **No witnessing structure is produced, so the question is unanswered.**

---

## Background

We work with countably infinite first-order structures whose universe is $\N$, interpreted
by computable constants/functions/relations (a *computable representation*). $\AUT(\A)$ is the
automorphism group. Two definitions from the problem:

- **Computably $\AUT$-countable on a cone.** There is $C\subseteq\N$ such that for every
  copy $\B\cong\A$, every $\sigma\in\AUT(\B)$ is computable from $\B\oplus C$.
- **$\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar a$.** There is a *family* of existential
  (computable-infinitary $\Sigma_1$) formulas $(\phi_i)_{i\in\N}$ with
  $f(x)=y \iff \exists i\,\A\models\phi_i(\bar a,x,y)$. Note: a *countable family*, not a
  single formula.

Cited results:

- **Theorem 2.2 (Hodges, *Model Theory* Cor. 4.2.5).** If $\A$ is countable and $\AUT(\A)$
  is countable, there is a *single* finite tuple $\bar a$ whose pointwise stabilizer is
  trivial — every automorphism is determined by its action on $\bar a$.
- **Theorem 2.3 (after Ash–Knight–Manasse–Slaman 1989).** $\A$ is computably $\AUT$-countable
  on a cone iff for **each** $\pi\in\AUT(\A)$ there is **some** finite $\bar a$ such that $\pi$
  is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar a$. The AKMS theorem: a relation is c.e.-on-a-cone
  iff it is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable with finitely many parameters; apply to graphs of
  automorphisms.

**Tool used by the solution (and correct):** *Preservation of existential formulas under
embeddings.* If $h:\B\hookrightarrow\B$ is a self-embedding (injective, preserving and
reflecting all relations) fixing $\bar c$ pointwise and $h(\pi(x_0))\neq\pi(h(x_0))$ for some
$x_0$, then $\pi$ is **not** $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar c$ (Lemma `lem:embcrit`).
This is the standard $\exists$-preservation theorem and is sound; it is the *correct* abstract
criterion for the negative clause and is the most valuable deliverable of the current draft.

**The conceptual heart (the Thm 2.2 / Thm 2.3 gap).** Theorem 2.2 gives ONE tuple that
*determines* every automorphism; Theorem 2.3 gives, for each $\pi$, a (possibly $\pi$-dependent)
tuple from which $\pi$ is effectively *definable*. Question 1.2 asks for a structure where the
"determine" power of one fixed tuple cannot be upgraded to "effectively define" — i.e. where
for every fixed $\bar a$ some $\pi$ resists $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definition even after the adversary
is handed $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$. A positive answer is a counterexample to a naive
effectivization of Theorem 2.2.

---

## Proof Structure

A complete solution to Question 1.2 requires a single computably-represented structure $\B$
with all of:

1. **(Framing)** $\B$ countable and $\AUT(\B)$ countable (so Thms 2.2/2.3 apply).
2. **(P1)** Every $\pi\in\AUT(\B)$ is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from *some* finite tuple
   (equivalently: $\B$ computably $\AUT$-countable on a cone). [Thm 2.3 direction.]
3. **(P2)** For *every* finite $\bar a$, there is $\pi\in\AUT(\B)$ that is **not**
   $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$.

The solution's Remark `rem:spec` correctly reduces (P2) to the *embedding form*:

> (ii) For every finite $\bar a$ there exist $\pi\in\AUT(\B)$ and a self-embedding $h$ of
> $\B$ fixing $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ pointwise with $h\circ\pi\neq\pi\circ h$.

(via Lemma `lem:embcrit`). A correct proof must also establish that **computability of the
representation, (P1), and (ii)** all hold of the *same* object — and either by direct coding
(e.g. via a non-c.e.-on-a-cone set $X$) or by a forcing/finite-injury diagonalization.

---

## Gap Analysis

The current draft is internally honest and largely correct on what it claims; its claims,
however, are insufficient to answer the question. The genuine gaps:

### Gap A (PRIMARY, blocking): No witnessing structure exists in the attempt.
The only concrete structure constructed (Definition `def:A`: gadgets $G_n=\{(n,i):i\in\Z\}$,
undirected path $P$ within gadgets, directed anchor $D$ on $G_0$, position-aligned directed
spine $R$) is **proved to fail (P2)** by the draft itself (Lemma `lem:leak`,
Corollary `cor:P2-fails`, Theorem `thm:G5`). The document then states the actual construction
is "left as the outstanding task." Thus the central existence assertion of Question 1.2 is
**entirely unproved**. Everything else in the file is preparatory.

I independently verified (finite truncation $0\le n\le4$, $|i|\le 6$) that:
- $\sigma_k(n,i)=(n,i+k)$ preserves $P,D,R$ on the interior (so $\sigma_k\in\AUT(\A)$), and
- the leak family $\phi_n$ of Lemma `lem:leak` defines $\sigma$ on the interior with the
  empty tuple (zero mismatches).
So the draft's negative conclusion about $\A$ is **correct**: $\A$ genuinely fails (P2).

### Gap B: The orientation-transmission tension is identified but not resolved.
Remark `rem:spec` argues (informally) that requirements (i)/(P1) and (ii)/(P2) are "in genuine
tension": any mechanism propagating a uniform orientation from finitely many anchored gadgets to
all gadgets (used to get P1 with a uniform $\Z$-shift) is "equally available to the adversary's
existential formulas," defeating (ii). This is presented as heuristic. **It is neither a proof
that the spine approach must fail in general, nor a proof that the question is positively
answerable.** The draft leaves open the crucial dichotomy:

- (B1) Is Question 1.2 answerable *yes* at all? No candidate survives in the file.
- (B2) Or might the "tension" be a genuine obstruction, so the answer is *no* (every computably
  $\AUT$-countable-on-a-cone structure admits, for some fixed $\bar a$, a uniform
  $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definition of all automorphisms from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$)? The draft does
  not address this possibility.

### Gap C: The framing must be re-established for any *new* construction.
The G2 lemmas (`lem:fix-index`, `lem:uniform`, `lem:translation`, `thm:aut`) are proved only for
the specific $\A$ of Definition `def:A`. They are **sound for that $\A$** (I checked the
in/out-degree argument for index recovery and the path-rigidity argument for translation), but
they buy nothing once $\A$ is discarded. Any replacement structure $\B$ needs its own complete
computation of $\AUT(\B)$ proving countability — and, by the tension in Gap B, must do so
*without* an orientation-transmitting spine. This is the hard part: keeping $\AUT(\B)$ countable
(forcing automorphisms to be "globally coordinated" enough that there are only countably many)
while keeping the coordination data *existentially invisible* from any externally-named
$\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$.

### Gap D (minor): An over-claim of finite-model "confirmation".
Lemma `lem:leak`'s parenthetical "(This is confirmed by a direct finite-model computation on the
truncation $0\le n\le4$, $|i|\le5$ …)" is acceptable as supporting evidence, but a finite
truncation introduces boundary points where $\bigvee_n\phi_n$ and $\mathrm{graph}(\sigma)$ may
differ; the proof must (and does, in the main text) rely on the infinite-model argument, not the
truncation. No correction needed, but the parenthetical should not be read as proof.

---

## Difficulty Assessment

- **Gap A / B is the entire research problem.** The difficulty is exactly the documented
  Thm 2.2 / Thm 2.3 gap. Resolving it requires *either*:
  - a genuinely new coupling mechanism that makes $\AUT(\B)$ countable while keeping the
    "which gadgets are flipped / how gadgets are coordinated" information $\Sigma^{in}_1$-
    invisible from any externally chosen finite tuple (plus its $\pi$-image); or
  - a theorem that no such $\B$ exists (a negative answer).
  Both directions are nontrivial descriptive-set-theory / computable-structure-theory results.

- **The handicap "$\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$" is what makes (P2) hard.** Handing the adversary the
  images $\pi(\bar a)$ may "spend gadget addresses" and, worse, may *reveal* the orientation of
  exactly those gadgets $\pi$ moves. The construction must guarantee that, for any finite
  $\bar a$, there remain infinitely many gadgets whose coordination is untouched by
  $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$, on which $\pi$ encodes non-$\Sigma^{in}_1$ information — and that a
  self-embedding fixing $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ can re-shuffle those gadgets non-commutingly
  with $\pi$ (the embedding form, Lemma `lem:embcrit`).

- **The countability constraint is in direct opposition.** Independent per-gadget $\Z/2$ choices
  give $(\Z/2)^{\N}$ (uncountable). Any device that collapses this to countably many
  automorphisms tends to *also* make the per-gadget choice definable — this is precisely the
  trap the draft fell into and then diagnosed. Threading countability without definability is
  the crux.

---

## Suggested Approaches

1. **Decouple "coordination" from "orientation transmission."** The fatal feature of $\A$ is
   that the spine $R$ is *directed and position-aligned*, so it both (a) coordinates gadgets
   (good, for countability) and (b) transmits a parameter-free orientation to every gadget
   (fatal, kills P2). Seek a coordination that fixes the gadget *indices* (countability) but
   leaves each gadget's internal orientation *undetermined by any existential formula over an
   external tuple*. Candidate ideas:
   - Make the coupling an *equivalence/parity* constraint rather than an oriented successor: e.g.
     encode only that gadgets $m,n$ are "flipped together" (a partition into finitely-determined
     blocks) without any directed edge that an existential witness can traverse to read an
     absolute orientation.
   - Ensure the only relations *internal* to and *incident* to each gadget are undirected, so
     that the orientation-reversing $\rho$ of Prop. `prop:K3` extends to a **self-embedding of
     all of $\B$** fixing any externally-chosen finite tuple — this is exactly condition (ii) of
     `rem:spec`. The proof obligation is then: such $\rho$ exists, fixes $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$,
     and does not commute with $\pi$.

2. **Directly target the embedding form (ii).** Design $\B$ so that for every finite $\bar a$
   there is a self-embedding $h$ with $h\restriction(\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a))=\mathrm{id}$ and
   $h\pi\neq\pi h$. Typically $h$ should be a "shift into unaddressed gadgets" or a "local
   reflection of a far gadget that is genuinely an embedding of the *whole* structure" (not just
   of a truncated substructure — the error the draft already diagnosed). The check that $h$ is a
   self-embedding of $\B$ (preserves and reflects ALL relations globally) is where the previous
   attempt collapsed; it must be done globally, not on an induced substructure.

3. **Coding a non-c.e.-on-a-cone set $X$** (per the route in issue prob-01-5). Let gadget $G_n$
   be "flipped" by the target $\pi$ iff $n\in X$ for a set $X$ that is not c.e. relative to the
   cone. Then a $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definition of $\pi$ from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ would, via the
   AKMS direction of Thm 2.3, yield a c.e.-on-a-cone description of $X$ (on the cofinitely many
   gadgets untouched by $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$), contradicting non-c.e.-ness. The subtlety:
   ensure (P1) still holds (each individual $\pi$ definable from *some* tuple — name a base
   point in each moved gadget) while (P2) holds against *fixed external* tuples.

4. **Seriously consider a negative answer.** Before more constructions, settle (B2): does the
   "orientation transmission = definability" tension generalize to a theorem? If every countable
   $\AUT$ with the right coordination is forced to make automorphisms uniformly definable, the
   answer to Question 1.2 is *no*, and the file's "tension" remark would be upgradable to a
   proof. A solver should attempt both a construction and a no-go argument in parallel.

5. **Re-derive the framing for the new $\B$.** Whatever $\B$ is chosen, a complete recomputation
   of $\AUT(\B)$ (proving countability) is mandatory — the G2 lemmas do not transfer.

---

## References

- **Prior issue-tracker work (read in full):**
  - `prob-01-1` (main): two prior critic reviews — initial analysis (no solution then existed)
    and a later verdict identifying the P1/P2 contradiction and witness-confinement error.
  - `prob-01-2` (G1): construct witnessing structure with computable copy (open).
  - `prob-01-4` (G3/P1): positive clause obligations (open).
  - `prob-01-5` (G4/P2): negative-clause diagonalization with the $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$
    handicap; suggests coding a non-c.e.-on-a-cone $X$ or finite-injury forcing (open).
  - `prob-01-6` (G5, in_progress): reconcile P1/P2 in the Thm 2.2/2.3 gap; solver comment
    confirms current $\A$ FAILS P2 via the orientation leak and supplies the embedding criterion.
  - `prob-01-7`: fatal P1/P2 contradiction for the spine construction (open).
  - `prob-01-8`: the witness-confinement error in the earlier P2 proof; $\rho$ is not a
    global automorphism (open).
  - (No `docs_*.md` / `docs_index.txt` files exist in the workspace; the referenced index is
    absent. SKILL.md present.)
- **Cited theorems:** Hodges, *Model Theory* (CUP 1993), Cor. 4.2.5 (Theorem 2.2);
  Ash–Knight–Manasse–Slaman 1989 (Theorem 2.3, c.e.-on-a-cone $\Leftrightarrow$
  $\Sigma^{in}_1$-with-parameters); $\exists$-formula preservation under embeddings
  (Łoś–Tarski direction used in Lemma `lem:embcrit`).
- **Numerical checks (this review):** finite truncation $0\le n\le4$, $|i|\le6$ confirms

## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

**Verdict: `solution.tex` does not answer Question 1.2.** Its mathematics is internally *correct*, but it studies only one concrete candidate $\A$ (Definition `def:A`: gadgets $G_n=\{(n,i):i\in\Z\}$; undirected in-gadget paths $P$; a directed anchor $D$ on $G_0$ only; a directed, position-aligned coupling spine $R:G_n\to G_{n+1}$) and **proves that this $\A$ FAILS the negative clause (P2)**, then explicitly defers the real construction.

### What is correct (not gaps)
- `lem:shifts-are-auts`–`thm:aut`: $\AUT(\A)\cong\Z$, $\sigma_k(n,i)=(n,i+k)$. The $R$-in/out-degree argument (sources $=G_0$), uniformity of the shift along rays, and killing of the reflection $f(i)=c-i$ by the directed anchor $D$ are all sound (checked).
- `lem:P1`: $\sigma^k$ is even **parameter-free** $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable via $\bigvee_n\theta_n^{(k)}$.
- `lem:leak`/`cor:P2-fails`: the spine $R$ plus anchor $D$ make orientation parameter-free definable, so **(P2) is false** for this $\A$. Correct.
- `rem:diagnosis`/`rem:K4-honest`: correctly **retract** the earlier invalid $\rho$-transport argument (the local reflection $\rho$ is an automorphism only of the induced substructure $\bar c\cup G_{n_0}$ with spine edges deleted; existential witnesses escape down the spine). Correct.

### Gaps (all already tracked — no duplicates filed)
1. **No witnessing structure produced.** The deliverable (a single $\A$ that is computable, has countable $\AUT$, and satisfies BOTH P1 and P2) is absent; the only concrete $\A$ provably fails P2. → prob-01-2, prob-01-9.
2. **P1↔P2 "tension" is heuristic only** (`rem:spec`): neither a YES construction nor a NO no-go theorem. → prob-01-9, prob-01-6, prob-01-7.
3. **P2 anti-uniform diagonalization unproved**, with the genuine handicap that parameters include the *images* $\pi(\bar a)$. → prob-01-5.
4. **P1 / "on a cone" (AKMS relativization)** must be re-established for any *corrected* candidate. → prob-01-4.
5. **Any P2 witness $h$ must be a GLOBAL self-embedding** (preserve+reflect ALL relations incl. coupling edges). → prob-01-10 (root cause: prob-01-8).

### Core difficulty (rigidity vs flexibility)
Keeping $\AUT$ countable forces a coupling that collapses $(\Z/2)^\N$/$D_\infty^\N$; but **any coupling that lets one anchored gadget orient all gadgets is equally available to the adversary's existential formulas, killing P2** — exactly what defeats the spine. Conversely, enough self-embeddings for the embedding criterion (`lem:embcrit`) tend to come from uncoupled local symmetries that blow $\AUT$ up to uncountable. The resolution must live **strictly inside the Theorem 2.2 / Theorem 2.3 gap**: orientation/swap-pattern *determined* by finitely many parameters (Thm 2.2, non-effective) yet **not** uniformly $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from one fixed external tuple (Thm 2.3).

### Recommended route
Replace the orienting spine by a **twin-pair / $\Z/2$ coding** template: gadgets with an involution swapping an existentially-indistinguishable twin pair; couple *only enough* to collapse $(\Z/2)^\N$ to a countable group (diagonal or finite-support) **without** a parameter-free existential orientation of individual twin pairs. Code a non-c.e.(-on-a-cone) set $X$ into the per-gadget swap so that a $\Sigma^{in}_1$ definition from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ would (via AKMS) compute $X$ — contradiction. The design must guarantee, for every finite $\bar a$, infinitely many gadgets both unaddressed by $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ and carrying genuine global-embedding flexibility. The spine satisfies "collapse $\AUT$" but **violates** "no parameter-free orientation" — precisely why it fails.

Full write-up attached as **Critic Analysis** (analysis.md). No `docs_*.md` files were present in the workspace; prior progress was read from issues prob-01-2,-4,-5,-6,-7,-8,-9,-10.

## Status: in_progress (not resolved). Honest report.

I worked the **top-level proof task** for Question 1.2 (does a computably AUT-countable-on-a-cone structure exist that fails the uniform-parameter effectivization of Thm 2.2?). I did **not** find a verified complete construction, so I am setting this to *in_progress* rather than overclaiming. What I rewrote into `solution.tex` is fully rigorous and self-consistent, with all automorphism-group computations and both refutations cross-checked numerically on finite truncations.

### What is now proved (complete proofs)
1. **Embedding criterion (Lemma).** If there is a self-embedding `h` fixing `c̄` pointwise with `h(π x₀) ≠ π(h x₀)` for some `x₀`, then `π` is not Σ^in₁-definable from `c̄`. (Existential formulas are preserved by embeddings.) This converts the negative clause (P2) into a statement about *proper self-embeddings*, and yields a clean **specification** (Cor.) for any positive answer.
2. **Candidate I (directed anchored spine).** AUT(A_I) ≅ ℤ, computed exactly. It satisfies (P1) but **fails (P2) at every tuple**: the directed spine R + anchor D make the generator σ Σ^in₁-definable with the *empty* parameter set (explicit family φ_n; numerically verified to equal graph(σ) on the interior of a 5×11 truncation). This also corrects the earlier draft's invalid "partial-reflection" proof of (P2).
3. **Candidate II (undirected coupling).** AUT(A_II) ≅ D_∞, computed exactly (tags pin gadget indices; undirected position-aligned R forces a single global sign+shift — verified combinatorially). It satisfies (P1) and **fails (P2) at every nonempty tuple**: for a translation, the labeled pair {a, π(a)} orients a gadget; for a reflection, {a,π(a)} (or a fixed center a) supplies the center, and reflections are symmetric so need no orientation (explicit geodesic family ψ_d; verified to equal the reflection graph). At the *empty* tuple A_II does admit a (P2)-witness (σ₁, via the reflection self-map and the embedding criterion), but since (P2) must hold for **every** finite tuple, A_II still fails.
4. **Obstruction lemma + Target spec.** Any *position-aligning* coupling strong enough to force AUT countable via a single global isometry (ℤ or D_∞) automatically transports the orienting/value datum along finite existential R-chains, defeating (P2). Hence a positive answer needs **(T1)** AUT countable but *not* a single global isometry — naturally a finite-support group like ⊕_n ℤ, with an automorphism that fixes any given `ā` yet acts on a disjoint "free" region (so `ā ∪ π(ā) = ā` is uninformative) — together with **(T2)** *proper* self-embeddings fixing `ā` that fail to commute with that π.

### The remaining blocker (precisely identified)
Realizing (T1) is the crux. Uncoupled translatable gadgets give AUT = ∏_n ℤ (uncountable); any position-aligning coupling that restores countability forces a single global isometry (obstruction lemma) and kills (T2). Forcing **finite support** (⊕_n, countable) *without pinning individual gadgets* is achieved by none of the naive devices I tried (a rigid backbone attached to a gadget origin pins that gadget and trivializes its automorphisms; loose attachments don't bound support). The bi-infinite line also has *no proper self-embeddings*, so (T2) needs a richer gadget. Decoupling "cofinitely many gadgets fixed" from "each gadget pinned," while supplying proper self-embeddings, is the open sub-problem.

### Suggested next step for collaborators
Construct a gadget that simultaneously (a) has nontrivial automorphisms, (b) admits proper self-embeddings fixing a prescribed finite set, and (c) couples into a structure whose AUT is ⊕_n (gadget-group) (finite support) rather than ∏_n. Then verify (T1)+(T2) via the embedding criterion. I believe the intended answer is YES (per the Background framing) but did not complete/verify it.
